stem: Which deliverable gives senior leaders a brief overview of the key findings and the recommended action from an analysis?

options.text: Executive summary
Self-service portal
Dynamic dashboard
Raw data extract

explanation: An executive summary condenses findings and a recommendation into a short read for leaders. A self-service portal is for users exploring data themselves, a dynamic dashboard supports ongoing interactive monitoring, and a raw extract gives detail with no interpretation.

stem: Business users at a retailer log in to a site where they browse approved datasets and build their own reports without filing a request. What is this delivery method called?

options.text: Static dashboard
Self-service portal
Executive summary
Recurring report

explanation: A self-service portal lets consumers find governed data and build their own views. A static dashboard is fixed content, an executive summary is a short narrative for leaders, and a recurring report is pushed on a schedule rather than built by the user.

stem: Which type of dashboard lets viewers apply filters, drill down into detail, and see data refreshed from its source?

options.text: Static dashboard
Snapshot report
Dynamic dashboard
Printed scorecard

explanation: A dynamic dashboard is interactive and connected to its data source. A static dashboard and a printed scorecard are fixed at the time they were produced, and a snapshot report deliberately freezes data at one point in time.

stem: Which data versioning technique captures the state of a dataset at a specific point in time so it can be referred to later?

options.text: Real-time streaming
In-place update
Live connection
Snapshot

explanation: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy kept for later reference. Real-time streaming and a live connection always show current values, and an in-place update overwrites old values so no history remains.

stem: Which TWO statements describe a static dashboard?

options.text: Its content is fixed when it is produced
Viewers can drill down into the details
It is often shared as a printed copy or image
It refreshes from the live data source
Viewers can apply their own filters

explanation: A static dashboard is a fixed rendering of data at production time and is commonly distributed as a printed copy or image. Drill-down, user filters and refresh from a live source are features of a dynamic dashboard.

stem: A payroll variance report is generated and emailed to department heads every Monday morning. Which delivery frequency is this?

options.text: Recurring
Ad hoc
Real-time
Exploratory

explanation: A report produced on a fixed schedule is recurring. Ad hoc reports answer one-off requests, real-time delivery updates continuously as data changes, and exploratory work is open-ended analysis rather than a delivery frequency.

stem: A manager asks once for the number of customers who used a discount code during last weekend's sale, and the question is not expected to come up again. Which delivery frequency fits?

options.text: Recurring
Ad hoc
Scheduled
Continuous

explanation: A one-time request answered when asked is ad hoc. Recurring and scheduled delivery repeat on a calendar, and continuous delivery keeps updating, which is wasted effort for a single question.

stem: With which data versioning approach do consumers see the latest values as soon as changes occur in the source?

options.text: Snapshot
Monthly archive
Real-time
Point-in-time copy

explanation: Real-time versioning reflects source changes as they happen. A snapshot, a monthly archive and a point-in-time copy all freeze data at a past moment.

stem: Ashgrove Insurance is replacing analyst-built reports with a self-service portal. Which TWO benefits should it expect?

options.text: Metric definitions no longer need an owner
A smaller backlog of routine report requests
No further need for access controls on data
No further need for data literacy training
Users can answer their own questions with governed data

explanation: Self-service lets users answer routine questions from governed data, which frees analysts from a backlog of simple requests. Governed metrics still need an owner, and self-service increases rather than removes the need for access controls and data literacy.

stem: A regional vice president has five minutes before a board meeting to learn the results of a 40-page customer churn study. What should the analyst provide?

options.text: The full study deck and appendix
A login to the self-service portal
An interactive dashboard with filters
A one-page executive summary

explanation: With five minutes, the reader needs the key findings and recommendation in a one-page executive summary. The full deck is too long, and a portal or interactive dashboard requires time to explore that the reader does not have.

stem: Store managers at Brightmere Grocers check sales against target several times a day and want to filter the figures by department. Which delivery method fits best?

options.text: A dynamic dashboard on the sales data
A static dashboard sent each month
An executive summary sent each quarter
A one-time ad hoc extract of sales

explanation: Frequent checks with department filters call for an interactive, refreshed dynamic dashboard. A monthly static report and a quarterly summary are too infrequent and cannot be filtered, and a one-time extract goes stale immediately.

stem: Auditors at Kestrel Bank need quarter-end balances exactly as they were reported on March 31, even though some entries were corrected in April. Which versioning technique supports this?

options.text: Real-time replication of the ledger
A snapshot taken at quarter close
A live view over the ledger tables
A streaming feed of journal entries

explanation: A quarter-close snapshot preserves the balances as reported, unaffected by later corrections. Real-time replication, a live view and a streaming feed all show current values, so the April corrections would overwrite what was reported.

stem: Which TWO situations are best served by real-time data rather than snapshots?

options.text: Year-end statements filed with a regulator
Flagging suspicious card transactions as they occur
Comparing this month with a frozen month-end baseline
Keeping a record of what a report showed last year
Routing warehouse pickers by current stock levels

explanation: Fraud flagging and live pick routing depend on the current state of the data, so real-time delivery fits. Filed statements, frozen baselines and historical records all need data fixed at a point in time, which snapshots provide.

stem: A compliance team must be able to reproduce exactly what a monthly sales report showed six months ago. What should be in place?

options.text: A dashboard that queries the live tables
A real-time streaming pipeline
Monthly snapshots of the report data
A self-service portal with edit rights

explanation: Monthly snapshots keep the data exactly as each report used it, so past reports can be reproduced. Live queries and streaming reflect today's values, and edit rights in a portal make past figures less reliable, not more.

stem: A marketing lead wants a one-time list of customers who bought from both product lines during a spring promotion. How should the analyst deliver it?

options.text: As a recurring daily report
As a scheduled weekly dashboard
As a standing monthly extract
As an ad hoc report

explanation: A single, one-time question is answered with an ad hoc report. Daily, weekly and monthly schedules would keep producing output that no one needs after the request is met.

stem: Hundreds of field sales reps at Corvane Supply need the same territory metrics every Monday. They do not need to interact with the data, and many work without a network connection. Which delivery fits best?

options.text: A recurring static report sent each Monday
A dynamic dashboard reached over the VPN
An ad hoc query that each rep runs on request
A real-time feed into each rep's spreadsheet

explanation: Fixed weekly metrics that must be readable offline suit a recurring static report. A dynamic dashboard over the VPN and a real-time feed need connectivity, and ad hoc queries repeat the same work for every rep each week.

stem: Which THREE features are characteristic of a dynamic dashboard?

options.text: Content frozen at the time of publishing
Filters and slicers the viewer can change
Delivery only as a printed handout
Drill-down from summary to detail
Values that cannot change once sent
Data refreshed from a connected source

explanation: Dynamic dashboards offer viewer-controlled filters, drill-down and refresh from a connected source. Frozen content, printed handouts and unchangeable values describe static delivery.

stem: A finance analyst receives requests from 30 managers who each want a slightly different cut of the same expense data. What is the best long-term delivery approach?

options.text: Build a separate static report for each manager
Publish the dataset through a self-service portal
Write one executive summary for all managers
Email a raw CSV extract each time someone asks

explanation: A self-service portal lets each manager slice governed data their own way without analyst effort per request. Thirty static reports are costly to maintain, a single summary cannot meet different needs, and repeated CSV extracts are ungoverned and keep the analyst busy.

stem: An analyst is writing an executive summary of a supplier cost study for the chief financial officer. Which content belongs in it?

options.text: The SQL queries used to build the data
Row-level detail for every invoice
Key findings, impact and a recommendation
A log of every data-cleaning step taken

explanation: An executive summary states the key findings, their business impact and the recommended action. Queries, cleaning logs and invoice-level detail belong in technical documentation or an appendix.

stem: A hospital operations center shows bed occupancy on wall screens, and staff need the display to reflect admissions within minutes. Which delivery fits best?

options.text: A daily snapshot loaded at midnight
A weekly static report posted Monday
A monthly executive summary for leaders
A dynamic dashboard on real-time data

explanation: Occupancy that must be current within minutes needs a dynamic dashboard fed by real-time data. A daily snapshot, a weekly report and a monthly summary would all show outdated occupancy.

stem: Which TWO are drawbacks of a static dashboard compared with a dynamic one?

options.text: It needs a live connection to open
It cannot be shared as a printed copy
Its data can go stale between issues
Each viewer needs a database license
Viewers cannot filter or drill down

explanation: A static dashboard is fixed when produced, so its data ages until the next issue and viewers cannot filter or drill down. It needs no live connection or database license, and it is commonly shared as a printed copy.

stem: A data science team must be able to retrain a model later on exactly the same data it was first trained on. How should the training data be managed?

options.text: Keep dated snapshots of the training data
Read it from live production tables
Stream new records into it continuously
Overwrite the training table each night

explanation: Dated snapshots preserve the exact data used, so training can be reproduced. Live tables, continuous streaming and nightly overwrites all change the data over time and lose the original version.

stem: Leaders at Orrin Telecom review yesterday's revenue at a 9 a.m. meeting, but the live dashboard keeps changing as late orders post. They want one stable figure for the discussion. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Switch the dashboard to faster real-time refresh
Present an end-of-day snapshot of yesterday's revenue
Add more filters to the live dashboard page
Remove the date filter from the live dashboard

explanation: A snapshot taken at the end of the day gives a fixed figure everyone can discuss. Faster refresh makes the number move more, and adding or removing filters does not stop live values from changing.

stem: At Halvard Freight, operations staff need live order status, while finance must reconcile to month-end figures that do not change after close. Which design meets both needs?

options.text: One real-time dataset feeding both groups' views
Month-end snapshots feeding both groups' views
Real-time for operations, snapshots for finance
Ad hoc extracts that each group requests as needed

explanation: Operations needs current status, so real-time data fits them, while finance needs frozen month-end figures, so snapshots fit them. A single real-time dataset breaks finance's reconciliation, snapshots alone leave operations with stale data, and ad hoc extracts meet neither need reliably.

stem: Before opening a self-service portal to 500 business users, which TWO controls matter most?

options.text: Role-based access to each dataset
Write access to source tables for all users
Turning off data refresh to reduce load
Certified datasets with documented metrics
Removing all prebuilt dashboards

explanation: Role-based access keeps users to the data they are allowed to see, and certified, documented datasets keep their reports consistent. Write access to sources risks damaging data, turning off refresh leaves users with stale data, and removing prebuilt dashboards takes away useful starting points.

stem: A static monthly dashboard goes to 40 managers, who keep sending follow-up questions such as "What does this look like for the West region only?" What is the best change?

options.text: Send the static dashboard weekly instead
Append every region's raw data to it
Write a longer executive summary
Make it dynamic with a region filter

explanation: The follow-ups ask for filtered views, which a dynamic dashboard with a region filter lets managers get themselves. Sending more often does not add filtering, raw appendices push the work onto readers, and a longer summary still cannot answer every region-specific question.

stem: A regulator asks Lindqvist Credit to show the customer risk ratings that drove a lending decision last April. The ratings table is updated in place every day. What is the problem, and what is the fix?

options.text: No history is kept; schedule point-in-time snapshots
The table is too large; archive it to cheaper storage
The dashboard is static; convert it to a dynamic view
Refresh is too slow; move the table to real-time

explanation: Updating in place overwrites old ratings, so April's values are gone; scheduled snapshots preserve them for the future. Archiving, dynamic views and real-time refresh address size, interactivity and speed, none of which recover or retain past values.

stem: A dashboard's only source is loaded in one batch each Sunday night. An analyst proposes refreshing the dashboard every minute so it is always current. What is the best response?

options.text: Keep the one-minute refresh to ensure freshness
Refresh once after the Sunday batch completes
Refresh hourly as a compromise between the two
Turn off refresh and update the page by hand

explanation: Refresh frequency should match how often the source changes, so a refresh after the weekly batch keeps the dashboard current at minimal cost. Minute-by-minute or hourly refreshes reload unchanged data and waste resources, and manual updates add error-prone work.

stem: Which TWO factors favor answering a request with an ad hoc report instead of building a recurring dashboard?

options.text: Many users need the same metric each week
Metrics must be tracked against targets over time
The question is expected to be asked only once
The data changes daily and must be monitored
The answer supports a single upcoming decision

explanation: A one-time question tied to a single decision does not justify building and maintaining a dashboard, so ad hoc delivery fits. Repeated weekly use, tracking against targets and ongoing monitoring are reasons to build a recurring dashboard.

stem: Regional managers at Penrose Outfitters compare store rankings at each quarter end, and later product returns must not change past quarters' figures. Which approach fits?

options.text: A real-time view of the sales table
A live connection with auto-refresh
Quarter-end snapshots of the rankings
Ad hoc queries run at each review

explanation: Quarter-end snapshots fix each quarter's rankings so later returns cannot alter them. A real-time view, a live connection and queries run at review time all pick up the later returns and change history.

stem: Users of a self-service portal are building reports that show different counts of "active customers" for the same month. What is the best fix?

options.text: Shut the portal and return to analyst-built reports
Give users direct access to the raw source tables
Require users to export data to spreadsheets first
Publish a certified dataset with one shared definition

explanation: Inconsistent counts come from users defining the metric differently, so a certified dataset with one shared definition fixes the cause. Closing the portal discards its benefits, and raw tables or spreadsheet exports make definitions diverge even more.

stem: Executives at Thornbury Mills only need monthly totals, but the dashboard they are given loads every transaction and takes minutes to open. Which delivery suits them better?

options.text: A monthly static dashboard of aggregated totals
A dynamic dashboard at transaction-level detail
A self-service portal over the raw tables
A real-time feed of every new transaction

explanation: An audience that needs monthly totals is best served by a light, aggregated monthly view. Transaction-level dashboards, raw-table portals and real-time feeds deliver detail the executives do not use and keep the slow load.

stem: An analyst at Wrenfield Charities must share annual program results with the board and with program staff who want to explore results for their own sites. Which TWO delivery choices fit?

options.text: Raw database credentials for board members
An executive summary for the board
An unfiltered transaction extract for the board
A real-time data stream sent to the board
Self-service portal access for program staff

explanation: The board needs a concise executive summary, and staff who want to explore their own sites need self-service access. Database credentials, raw extracts and real-time streams give the board detail and tooling it will not use.

stem: What is the main advantage of a dynamic dashboard over a static one?

options.text: It gives a fixed record of the results
Viewers can explore current data themselves
It prints without any loss of detail
It needs no connection to a data source

explanation: Dynamic dashboards let viewers filter and drill into data that refreshes from the source. A fixed record, clean printing and no source connection are traits of static delivery.

stem: Gate agents at Skyvale Air need to see delays and gate changes the moment they are entered. Which data versioning approach should feed their display?

options.text: Nightly snapshot
Weekly static report
Real-time feed
Monthly archive

explanation: Changes that must appear immediately need a real-time feed. A nightly snapshot, weekly report and monthly archive would show agents outdated gate information.

stem: A KPI dashboard is issued as a fixed report at each month end and is also available as a dynamic dashboard. Board members notice last month's revenue differs between the two. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The fixed report uses a different chart type
The dynamic version has more filters
The fixed report was rendered at low resolution
Source data was revised after the report

explanation: The fixed report froze values at month end, while the dynamic dashboard picks up later revisions to the source, so the figures diverge. Chart type and resolution do not change values, and extra filters would not explain a difference in the same unfiltered total.

stem: Which TWO statements about snapshot versioning are accurate?

options.text: It shows source changes as soon as they occur
It preserves the state of data at a point in time
It requires a streaming pipeline to capture
It lets analysts reproduce past reports exactly
It uses less storage than keeping no history

explanation: A snapshot freezes data at a point in time, so past reports can be reproduced from it. Showing changes as they occur and relying on streaming describe real-time delivery, and keeping snapshots adds storage rather than saving it.

stem: Match each audience need to the best delivery method.

prompts.text: Board members want one page of conclusions
Staff look up their own region whenever they like
The same sales report goes out every Monday
A finance director asks a one-time question about a promotion

explanation: Executives need short conclusions, portals let users find their own data, a fixed schedule makes a report recurring, and a one-time question is ad hoc. A static dashboard is a format, not a match for any of these needs.

partExplanations.p1: A one-page conclusion is an executive summary.
partExplanations.p2: Looking up data on demand is self-service.
partExplanations.p3: A fixed weekly schedule is recurring.
partExplanations.p4: A one-time request is ad hoc.

stem: Match each description to the term it defines.

prompts.text: Figures frozen as of midnight on quarter end
Figures that update as events arrive
A dashboard whose viewers can filter and drill down
A dashboard saved with fixed values that cannot be changed by the viewer

explanation: A snapshot preserves data at a point in time, while real-time data keeps changing. Dynamic dashboards respond to the viewer, and static ones do not. An executive summary is a content style and defines none of these.

partExplanations.p1: Frozen at a moment is a snapshot.
partExplanations.p3: Filtering and drill-down make a dashboard dynamic.
partExplanations.p4: Fixed values make a dashboard static.

stem: Sort each feature by the kind of dashboard it describes.

items.text: Printed and handed out at a meeting
Saved as an image with fixed numbers
Click a region to drill into its stores
Viewer sees new figures without anyone republishing it
Figures stay as they were at publication

explanation: Static dashboards are fixed at publication, such as prints and images. Dynamic ones respond to filters, drilling and refreshes.

partExplanations.i2: Changing a date range needs interactivity.
partExplanations.i5: New figures appearing without republishing is dynamic behavior.

stem: Put the steps of setting up a recurring weekly report in order.

steps.text: Confirm who reads the report and what they decide with it
Review a sample with the main reader
Connect and prepare the data source

explanation: Requirements come first, then data, then design. The reader approves a sample before the schedule is switched on.

partExplanations.s3: Visuals are built on the prepared data.

stem: Put the steps of writing an executive summary in order.

steps.text: Link to the detailed dashboard for anyone who wants more
State the main conclusion in one sentence
Recommend the action the reader should take
Back it up with two or three key numbers before any recommendation

explanation: Executives read the conclusion first, then the evidence, then what to do, with detail available but out of the way.

stem: Supervisors in a call center need a screen showing the current waiting queue that they can filter by team. Finance also needs a frozen copy of month-end figures for audit. Configure the delivery.

fields.label: Type of dashboard for the supervisors

options.text: Static dashboard
Dynamic dashboard
Executive summary
Snapshot
Real-time

fields.label: Data currency for the month-end audit copy

options.text: Snapshot
Real-time

explanation: Filtering by team needs a dynamic dashboard, and a live queue needs real-time data. An audit copy must not change afterwards, so it is a snapshot.

partExplanations.version: A current queue must update continuously.
partExplanations.audit: An audit copy has to stay fixed.

stem: Label each stage of this reporting flow with the term that fits.

nodes.text: Holds every order as it is entered
One page of conclusions for the board

explanation: The source system holds live records, a snapshot freezes them, a portal lets users help themselves, and an executive summary condenses the result. A real-time feed would not be a frozen copy.

partExplanations.z1: Where orders are entered is the source system.
partExplanations.z2: A frozen nightly copy is a snapshot.
partExplanations.z3: Staff finding their own data is self-service.
partExplanations.z4: One page for the board is an executive summary.
